Single-ordering CAVI

Source: vignettes/cavi_single.Rmd
cavi_single.Rmd

This page describes coordinate-ascent variational inference (CAVI) for the single-ordering model. The tutorial presents the model and a fitting example; this page gives the objective, posterior updates, empirical-Bayes updates, and stopping rule.

There are n samples, d features, and K ordered grid positions. Sample i occupies position c_i, feature j has trajectory \boldsymbol{u}_j, and Q_K is the random-walk precision matrix. The position prior is \Pr(c_i=k)=\pi_k, observation variance is \sigma_j^2, and smoothness precision is \lambda_j.

Variational objective

fit_mpcurve() alternates between updates of the posterior distributions and model parameters to maximize the evidence lower bound (ELBO). Write r_{ik} := q_i(c_i = k), \qquad N_k := \sum_{i=1}^n r_{ik}, and for each feature j, q_j(\boldsymbol{u}_j) = N(\boldsymbol{m}_j, S_j).

Under the mean-field family q(C,U)=\prod_{i=1}^n q_i(c_i)\prod_{j=1}^d q_j(\boldsymbol{u}_j), the ELBO can be written, up to additive constants, as \mathcal L(q) = \sum_{i=1}^n\sum_{k=1}^K r_{ik}\log \pi_k - \sum_{i=1}^n\sum_{k=1}^K r_{ik}\log r_{ik} - \frac12 \sum_{i=1}^n\sum_{k=1}^K\sum_{j=1}^d r_{ik} \left[ \log(2\pi \sigma_j^2) + \frac{(x_{ij}-m_{jk})^2 + S_{j,kk}}{\sigma_j^2} \right] + \frac12 \sum_{j=1}^d \left[ \operatorname{rank}(Q_K)\log \lambda_j - \lambda_j\Big(\boldsymbol{m}_j^\top Q_K \boldsymbol{m}_j + \operatorname{tr}(Q_K S_j)\Big) + \log |S_j| \right].

This objective, including its additive constants, is recorded in elbo_trace. For the intrinsic prior, normalization uses the rank and generalized determinant of Q_K, with a fixed reference measure on its null space. It provides a within-model fitting objective. The updates below maximize it one block at a time, with estimated noise, adaptive position probabilities, and no additional smoothness-parameter prior. Parameter estimates are restricted to the configured bounds.

Trajectory distributions

Fix r_{ik}, \sigma_j^2, and \lambda_j. The ELBO terms involving \boldsymbol{u}_j are quadratic, so the optimal variational factor is Gaussian: \log q_j^\star(\boldsymbol{u}_j) = -\frac12 \boldsymbol{u}_j^\top A_j \boldsymbol{u}_j + \boldsymbol{u}_j^\top \boldsymbol{b}_j + \text{const}, where A_j = \lambda_j Q_K + \operatorname{diag}\!\left(N_1/\sigma_j^2,\dots,N_K/\sigma_j^2\right), and b_{jk} = \frac{1}{\sigma_j^2}\sum_{i=1}^n r_{ik} x_{ij}. Therefore, S_j = A_j^{-1}, \qquad \boldsymbol{m}_j = S_j \boldsymbol{b}_j.

The diagonal likelihood term supplies information at the grid positions, while the random-walk precision shares information between neighboring positions. Their combination determines both the fitted trajectory and its uncertainty.

Sample positions

Fix q(U), \pi, and \sigma_j^2. Collecting the ELBO terms involving the row r_{i\cdot} gives \log r_{ik} = a_i + \log \pi_k - \frac12 \sum_{j=1}^d \left[ \log(2\pi \sigma_j^2) + \frac{(x_{ij}-m_{jk})^2 + S_{j,kk}}{\sigma_j^2} \right]. So the cell-position posterior is updated by a row-wise softmax: r_{i\cdot} \leftarrow \operatorname{softmax}\!\big(\ell_{i1},\dots,\ell_{iK}\big), with \ell_{ik} equal to the position-specific terms above and a_i the normalizing constant.

The S_{j,kk} term accounts for trajectory uncertainty when assigning a sample to a grid position.

Position probabilities

Fixing everything else, we maximize \sum_{k=1}^K N_k \log \pi_k subject to \sum_k \pi_k = 1. A Lagrange multiplier gives \pi_k = \frac{N_k}{n}.

Noise variances

Fixing q(U) and q(C), differentiate the ELBO with respect to \sigma_j^2. The stationary point is \sigma_j^2 = \frac{1}{n} \sum_{i=1}^n \sum_{k=1}^K r_{ik}\Big[(x_{ij}-m_{jk})^2 + S_{j,kk}\Big].

So each feature variance is updated from the posterior expected residual sum of squares.

Smoothness precisions

Fixing q(U), only the prior part of the ELBO depends on \lambda_j: \frac12 \operatorname{rank}(Q_K)\log \lambda_j - \frac12 \lambda_j \Big(\boldsymbol{m}_j^\top Q_K \boldsymbol{m}_j + \operatorname{tr}(Q_K S_j)\Big). Setting the derivative to zero yields \lambda_j = \frac{\operatorname{rank}(Q_K)} {\boldsymbol{m}_j^\top Q_K \boldsymbol{m}_j + \operatorname{tr}(Q_K S_j)}.

Assessing convergence

Each update maximizes one objective block while holding the others fixed, so elbo_trace should be nondecreasing up to numerical tolerance. A plateau indicates that successive iterations are making small improvements. Because the objective can have multiple optima, compare several initializations when the trajectory is complex or weakly identified.

By default, fitting stops when the absolute ELBO change divided by N * D is below 1e-6, where N is the number of samples and D the number of features. The same tol applies to single and multiple orderings. Fitting uses temperature T = 1 throughout by default; optional partition annealing can be enabled through mpcurve_control(anneal_steps = 25, anneal_start = 5). Convergence is assessed at T = 1. The objective must also satisfy the algorithm’s numerical nondecrease check. Setting tol to zero disables early stopping.

control = mpcurve_control(convergence = "relative") selects the previous ELBO-relative rule. The tolerance remains controlled by tol. do_mpcurve() inherits the rule and tolerance stored in the fit; saved fits without a rule retain relative stopping. Stored ELBO traces are unchanged. A small increment indicates slow improvement, not a bound on the remaining optimization error.

Return to the fitting example. For multiple orderings and soft feature assignments, see Multi-ordering CAVI.
